title: Limited Attention: Implications for Financial Reporting

scopes.description: The assessed target is the as-downloaded online appendix's supplementary theoretical analyses, proofs, and six numerical figures. This one-file release supplies mathematical content but no executable computational workflow. The scope does not infer the main article's unprovided empirical or paper-wide analyses; the appendix's main-text references remain an explicit context gap.

issues.description: The assigned inventory contains only this mathematical online appendix. It reports numerical verification and presents six figures with some captioned parameter settings, but supplies no executable program, launch driver, identified software, or complete numerical reproduction procedure. Equations and proof derivations are model content, not an executable program. The appendix figures and numerical claims therefore cannot be rerun from this package alone.

The appendix refers to Section 4 and Section 2 of the main text for model setup and proof expressions, but the frozen package contains only the online appendix. The exact referenced definitions are needed to interpret the supplementary material in context; no substitute definitions are inferred.

evidence.description: The appendix says the bank-run attention conjecture is verified numerically and states Figure 4 settings.
evidence.quote:
The conjecture is verified numerically. In Figure 4 below, I plot creditor i’s incentive
to deviate to the summary as a function of C, when σγ2 = 1.5 and δ = 1. The plot

indeed shows that the larger C is, the lower the incentive to deviate. Hence, when C
is sufficiently large, we expect an equilibrium where all creditors divide their attention
evenly between the two details.

actions.description: Request the authors' actual computational source or a complete documented manual/computational recipe for the appendix's IPO and bank-run numerical verifications and Figures 1–6, plus the cited main-text model definitions required to interpret them. Do not substitute a new solver or reconstruct the research from equations.
steps: Request the original program or the authors' complete actual numerical procedure and run instructions for the appendix's numerical claims and six figures.

Ask the authors to identify the software/version and any actual parameter grids, evaluation/optimization settings, and required inputs used, where applicable; the existing figure captions' stated parameter values are preserved as supplied.
Obtain the referenced Section 2 and Section 4 model definitions from the main text if they are not already supplied with the reproducibility materials.
Once supplied, inspect the actual source and dependencies, order its documented steps, and reassess required inputs and readiness before any separately authorized execution.
validation: Confirm each appendix numerical claim and Figures 1–6 maps to an actual supplied entry point or documented manual step, with all required model definitions and inputs accounted for.
Keep execution unverified until a separately authorized run checks the author's outputs.

review_notes: Scope is limited to the sole as-downloaded online appendix in the frozen inventory. The title is consistent with the registered frozen header; no DOI conflict appears in the supplied source.

The full cached appendix (lines 1–906) was read. Its equations, parameter statements, proofs, and numerical-verification prose are not treated as runnable code. The six figure captions do state parameters, so the assessment does not claim those settings are absent because of PDF text extraction.

No empirical dataset, named software/product, author code, or author numerical recipe is supplied in this package. No empirical data requirement or analysis-only scope is invented; no catalog/product lookup was required because the source names no required product.

No original-page render, model solution, numeric calculation, software probe, author contact, or broader package scan was performed. The static audit is cited only as a discovery aid; the direct complete source review supports the code-presence finding.
